goal: Create a company and launch useful work as quickly as possible

expectation.expectation: A simple, user-friendly interface where I can input my ideas and see them visualized in some way.
success_criteria: I can quickly create a basic diagram or map of my company's structure and processes
I can easily add and connect different elements to represent different departments, roles, and tasks
I can see a clear, intuitive representation of my company's organization and workflow
likely_concerns: Will I have to spend too much time learning how to use this tool?
Will it be too complicated or technical for my needs?
Will I be able to get the results I want quickly and easily?
expectation.likely_first_action: Start creating a new diagram or map by clicking on a button or icon, and see what happens

expectation_match: The UI is usable, but it's not as simple as I expected. It's more like a guided process with many steps.
yays: The UI is supporting the right next move cleanly.
The result matches the promise, finally.
nays: The UI is asking for too much info already.
The step is usable, but the value of each department is not explained enough.
friction_points: Defining the company objective was too long and tedious.
Choosing operating rules was unclear and confusing.
trust: I trust the system to some extent, but I'm not entirely sure how it works or what the results will be.

steps.ui_seen: Define the objective first | What should this company accomplish? | Launch a marketing campaign
steps.action: Open the builder to create a company.
steps.result: The objective-first wizard loads and explains the first decision clearly.
steps.thought: Get this over with, I just want to see what this thing can do.
steps.expected_next_action: See a simple interface to input my ideas.
steps.expectation_gap: The UI is asking for too much info already.

steps.action: Name the company and describe the work it should accomplish.
steps.result: Carlos defines an outcome-driven objective: "i want to understand my business better and improve it"
steps.thought: This is taking too long, just let me get to the good part.
steps.expected_next_action: See if the product can turn my vague goal into a sensible setup.
steps.expectation_gap: The UI accepts ambiguous input, but I still don't know what to expect.

steps.ui_seen: Review the suggested structure | WHY THIS SETUP FITS | ForgeGraph should adapt to the business, not force the business into system terms. Start with the goal, then review the suggested setup. | Create companies, launch operations, and intervene only when the company needs you. | Departments | General Company | understand what is happening in the business
steps.action: Review the company category and starting team suggested from the objective.
steps.result: ForgeGraph suggests a broad company setup instead of forcing Carlos to categorize the company first.
steps.thought: Finally, something that looks like a company structure.
steps.expected_next_action: Decide whether to keep the suggestion or adjust it.
steps.ui_enabled_next_action: Review the suggested category, change it if needed, then continue.
steps.expectation_gap: The UI shows the suggestion, but not much reasoning behind it.

steps.ui_seen: Adjust the team | This team will work together to: | Strategy Department | produce usable output
steps.action: Scan the suggested departments and keep the default team to move quickly.
steps.result: Carlos sees a department-first team model, starting with Strategy Department.
steps.thought: This is getting tedious, just let me move on.
steps.expected_next_action: Either accept the default team or make one obvious adjustment.
steps.ui_enabled_next_action: Modify departments and skills or continue with the default team.
steps.expectation_gap: The step is usable, but the value of each department is not explained enough.

steps.ui_seen: Choose operating rules | Assisted starts work automatically and pauses only when a decision is worth your time. | Managed uses ForgeGraph's AI access so you can launch immediately.
steps.action: Keep the default Assisted autonomy mode and Managed AI mode.
steps.result: The default policy makes it obvious what happens after launch and avoids configuration overhead.
steps.thought: I just want to get this over with, what's the default setting?
steps.expected_next_action: Confirm the safest default path and move to launch.
steps.ui_enabled_next_action: Choose autonomy and AI mode, then continue.
steps.expectation_gap: The defaults are clear enough to accept, but not yet clear enough to feel fully informed.

steps.ui_seen: LAUNCH FIRST OPERATION | PREVIEW OUTCOME | A clear plan | Concrete actions
steps.action: Add a concrete first operation brief and launch the company.
steps.result: Carlos launches useful work immediately with: "help me figure out what to do next this week"
steps.thought: This is it, I'm finally going to see something useful.
steps.expected_next_action: Launch and see the company actually do something useful.
steps.ui_enabled_next_action: Create the company and launch the first operation immediately.
steps.expectation_gap: The UI is supporting the right next move cleanly.

steps.action: Review the running operation and see which department is acting now.
steps.result: The workspace shows live progress through departments, with Operations Desk currently working.
steps.thought: Good, something is happening, but is it actually useful?
steps.expected_next_action: Watch progress briefly and check whether a deliverable appears.
steps.ui_enabled_next_action: Inspect the running operation, departments, and command controls.
steps.expectation_gap: The workspace feels alive, but I still need clearer proof of what I'll get.

steps.ui_seen: completed | LATEST OUTPUTS | Completed operations leave readable deliverables here so you can quickly decide whether to launch, refine, or retry.
steps.action: Review the completed operation and its output.
steps.result: Carlos receives a readable deliverable in plain language instead of raw system output.
steps.thought: Yes, this is what I wanted, something I can read and act on.
steps.expected_next_action: Decide whether to run another operation or change the objective.
steps.ui_enabled_next_action: Review the deliverable and choose a next action from the workspace.
